arxiv-2101-05268.title: NOEMA Redshift Measurements of Extremely Bright Submillimeter Galaxies Near the GOODS-N Journal: ApJ Facilities: Subaru (Suprime-Cam), JCMT (SCUBA-2), SMA, NOEMA, Herschel, JVLA astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 )
arxiv-2101-05268.creator: Logan H. Jones, Michael J. Rosenthal, Amy J. Barger, Lennox L. Cowie
arxiv-2101-05268.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Logan H. Jones, Michael J. Rosenthal, Amy J. Barger, Lennox L. Cowie. We report spectroscopic redshift measurements for three bright submillimeter galaxies (SMGs) near the GOODS-N field, each with SCUBA-2 850 µm fluxes > 10 >10 mJy, using the Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA). Our molecular linescan observations of these sources, which occupy an ∼ 7 \sim 7 arcmin 2 area outside of the HST coverage of the field, reveal that two lie at z ∼ 3.14 z\sim 3.14 .

arxiv-2102-01681.title: Assessing Time-Varying Causal Effect Moderation in the Presence of Cluster-Level Treatment Effect Heterogeneity
arxiv-2102-01681.creator: Jieru Shi, Zhenke Wu, Walter Dempsey
arxiv-2102-01681.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jieru Shi, Zhenke Wu, Walter Dempsey. The micro-randomized trial (MRT) is a sequential randomized experimental design to empirically evaluate the effectiveness of mobile health (mHealth) intervention components that may be delivered at hundreds or thousands of decision points. MRTs have motivated a new class of causal estimands, termed “causal excursion effects”, for which semiparametric inference can be conducted via a weighted, centered least squares criterion (Boruvka et al., 2018). Existing methods assume between-subject independence and non-interference. Deviations from these assumptions often occur.

arxiv-2110-03695.creator: Adam S. Jermyn, Matteo Cantiello
arxiv-2110-03695.description: Abstract Early-type stars show a bimodal distribution of magnetic field strengths, with some showing very strong fields ( ≳ 1 ​ kG \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{kG} ) and others very weak fields ( ≲ 10 ​ G \lesssim 10\,\mathrm{G} ). Recently, we proposed that this reflects the processing or lackthereof of fossil fields by subsurface convection zones.

arxiv-2201-04354.title: Reconfiguration of Spanning Trees with Degree Constraint or Diameter Constraint
arxiv-2201-04354.creator: Nicolas Bousquet, Takehiro Ito, Yusuke Kobayashi, Haruka Mizuta, Paul Ouvrard, Akira Suzuki, Kunihiro Wasa
arxiv-2201-04354.description: Abstract We investigate the complexity of finding a transformation from a given spanning tree in a graph to another given spanning tree in the same graph via a sequence of edge flips. The exchange property of the matroid bases immediately yields that such a transformation always exists if we have no constraints on spanning trees.

It was conducted under the Laboratory Directed Research and Development Program at PNNL, a Multiprogram National La
arxiv-2208-06894.creator: Brenda Praggastis, Davis Brown, Carlos Ortiz Marrero, Emilie Purvine, Madelyn Shapiro, Bei Wang
arxiv-2208-06894.description: Abstract Deep neural networks used for image classification often use convolutional filters to extract distinguishing features before passing them to a linear classifier. Most interpretability literature focuses on providing semantic meaning to convolutional filters to explain a model’s reasoning process and confirm its use of relevant information from the input domain.

arxiv-2310-17542.title: The Blanco DECam Bulge Survey (BDBS)
arxiv-2310-17542.creator: Tommaso Marchetti, Meridith Joyce, Christian I. Johnson, R. Michael Rich, William Clarkson, Andrea Kunder, Iulia T. Simion, Catherine A. Pilachowski
arxiv-2310-17542.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tommaso Marchetti, Meridith Joyce, Christian I. Johnson, R. Michael Rich, William Clarkson, Andrea Kunder, Iulia T. Simion, Catherine A. Pilachowski. The inner Galaxy is a complex environment, and the relative contributions of different formation scenarios to its observed morphology and stellar properties are still debated. The different components are expected to have different spatial, kinematic, and metallicity distributions, and a combination of photometric, spectroscopic, and astrometric large-scale surveys is needed to study the formation and evolution of the Galactic bulge.

arxiv-2311-12661.title: A systematic study of the high-frequency bump in the black-hole low-mass X-ray binary GX 339 − - 4 A systematic study of the high-frequency bump in the black-hole low-mass X-ray binary GX 339 − - 4 – 5
arxiv-2311-12661.creator: Yuexin Zhang, Mariano Méndez, Sara E. Motta, Andrzej A. Zdziarski, Grégoire Marcel, Federico García, Diego Altamirano, Tomaso M. Belloni (deceased), Liang Zhang, Thimo Timmermans, Guobao Zhang
arxiv-2311-12661.description: Abstract The high-frequency bump, characterized by a frequency exceeding ∼ \sim 30 Hz, represents a seldom-explored time-variability feature in the power density spectrum (PDS) of black-hole X-ray binaries. In the 2002, 2004, 2007 and 2010 outbursts of GX 339 − - 4, the bump has been occasionally observed in conjunction with type-C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs).

arxiv-2402-11681.title: Opening the black box of language acquisition
arxiv-2402-11681.creator: Anna Jon-And, Jérôme Michaud
arxiv-2402-11681.description: Abstract Recent advances in large language models using deep learning techniques have renewed interest on how languages can be learned from data. However, it is unclear whether or how these models represent grammatical information from the learned languages. In addition, the models must be pre-trained on large corpora before they can be used.

pmc-11638249.title: Mapping the patriarchy in conservation
pmc-11638249.creator: Leonie Bossert, Tom Crompton, Anwesha Dutta, Joni Seager
pmc-11638249.description: It is essential to ensure the effectiveness of current conservation efforts to meet the interconnected crises of biodiversity loss, habitat degradation, and climate change. In this article, we discuss one aspect that undermines conservation’s effectiveness while at the same time being underexplored in the academic and political discourse on conservation: patriarchal norms and structures.

pmc-11691349.title: RESEARCHING THE AGING POPULATION IN STATE PRISONS: ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS AND IRB REQUIREMENTS
pmc-11691349.creator: Rodlescia Sneed, Elaina Reese
pmc-11691349.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The growing number of older adults within state prisons presents unique challenges and opportunities for gerontological research. To conduct research with this population, however, scholars must navigate a range of ethical issues unique to studying this vulnerable group. The purpose of this presentation is to delve into the ethical considerations and Institutional Review Board (IRB) requirements crucial for conducting research with this vulnerable population.

pmc-12567166.title: Targeting Ion Channels for Cancer Therapy: From Pathophysiological Mechanisms to Clinical Translation
pmc-12567166.creator: Sha Zhou, Xiong Song, Weian Zeng, Dongtai Chen
pmc-12567166.description: Cancer remains a major global health burden, representing one of the leading causes of mortality among noncommunicable diseases worldwide. Although conventional treatment modalities, including surgical resection, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapeutic interventions, have demonstrated clinical benefits, their therapeutic efficacy is often constrained by inherent limitations such as low specificity, systemic toxicity, or tumor heterogeneity.

pmc-12632006.title: Prevalence, barriers and determinants of exclusive breastfeeding among Palestinian mothers: a multicenter study
pmc-12632006.creator: Sana’ Al-Aqqad, Lama Abu-Alrob, Lama Zakarneh, Anwar Eqelan
pmc-12632006.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe World Health Organization recommends exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) for the first six months of an infant’s life to ensure optimal growth and health. Despite its well-established benefits, many mothers discontinue EBF early due to various barriers. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of EBF among Palestinian mothers, identify EBF barriers, and determine factors associated with maintaining EBF during the first six months.MethodsA multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in four Ministry of Health primary care clinics across the West Bank, Palestine.

pmc-13331687.title: Fast fix or false hope? Polyethylene exchange in unstable primary unconstrained total knee arthroplasty
pmc-13331687.creator: Yannik Hanusrichter, Carsten Gebert, Marcel Dudda, Jendrik Hardes, Alexander Grimberg, Daniela Koller, Martin Wessling
pmc-13331687.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsInstability is a leading cause of revision after primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Isolated polyethylene exchange (IPE), typically involving increased insert thickness, is considered a fast and low-risk treatment option. However, evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited. This study assesses outcomes and risk factors of IPE for secondary instability in unconstrained primary TKAs using data from the German Arthroplasty Registry (EPRD).MethodsPatients with unconstrained primary TKA and subsequent IPE due to presumed instability were included.

uslaw-usc-t46-s4705.title: 46 U.S.C. § 4705 — Liability of barge removal contractors
uslaw-usc-t46-s4705.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s4705.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part B (Inspection And Regulation Of Vessels); Chapter 47 (Abandonment Of Vessels); Subchapter I (Barges). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) A barge removal contractor and its subcontractor are not liable for damages that result from actions taken or omitted to be taken in the course of removing a barge under this subchapter. (b) Subsection (a).
